correctness.rationale: An edge-open packing S has endpoint-induced graph consisting of nontrivial star components: an unselected joining edge or a four-vertex path contradicts the third-edge exclusion. Conversely such an induced star forest yields a unique S. Canonical selected vertex degree 0/1/>=2 prevents multiplicities (even for K2). Five parent interfaces separate unselected, leaf with selected parent, leaf without selected parent, center with unselected parent, center with selected leaf parent. The specific a,b,h,c,d recurrences in inspected RESULT.md enumerate these classes and attach each parent-child selected edge with exactly one z. Root uses a+h+c; connected components multiply. Induction proves all n, not the finite tests. Independent fresh brute-force third-edge checks on P5, K1,4 and six-vertex fork produced polynomials [1,4,4], [1,4,6,4,1], [1,5,6,2], equal to a separate implementation of the 5-state recurrence. O(n^3) counts polynomial arithmetic not bit complexity.
residual_risks: Unindexed explicit all-coefficient tree-DP may exist, even if scalar results do not imply it.

value.rationale: The studied natural packing invariant has an all-cardinality distribution, number of optimal solutions, and counting recurrence beyond the known extremal scalar. A canonical state decomposition for every forest is independently useful and not an arbitrary single-graph computation; practical polynomial-time arithmetic produces coefficient multiplicities.
residual_risks: Arithmetic operation complexity does not bound output bit length; excludes graphs with cycles.

final_claim: For every finite simple forest F, including empty/isolated vertices, the edge-open-packing generating polynomial P_F(z)=sum_{valid S subset E(F)} z^{|S|} is exactly computed by a disjoint five-state rooted recursion in O(n^3) integer-arithmetic operations for n vertices.
